title: Macro Friendly Crispy Chicken Sandwich  Per sandwich: 440 Calories 50g Protein* 43g Carbs 6g Fat Weight: ~12 ounces  Chick-fil-A Version: 440 calories 29g Protein 41g Carbs 17g Fat Weight: ~6.5 ounces  In other words - my version is DOUBLE the size, almost double the protein, 1/3 the fat content, for the same calories as the chick fil a sandwich. And in my opinion - it tastes much better too  *Also - in the video I said it contains “almost 50g of protein” 😅 - because I forgot to include the sauce in the initial macro calculation. The sriracha sauce adds ~5g of protein to each sandwich!  Ingredients:  One ~12oz chicken breast, halved  Salt + garlic powder  **Dipping stations** Station 1: Flour + salt/garlic/pepper Station 2: Egg whites + hot sauce Station 3: Crushed corn flakes  NOTE: I don’t measure the amount of each ingredient added to each station as it’s typically easier to add excess in order to ensure complete coating. I weighed the amount that stuck to each piece of chicken in order to calculate the macronutrients. Flour: 5g per Cornflakes: 15g per Egg white + hot sauce adds virtually no calories (maybe 2-3 Cals)  1 toasted brioche bun (mine was 160 calories, use any preferred bun)  Sauce: 90g fat free plain Greek yogurt 30g Sriracha 5g Gochujang (optional) 2 spoonfuls of pickle juice  Pickles of choice  #chickensandwich #chickfilarecipe #crispychickensandwich #crispychickensandwichrecipe #healthyrecipes #healthyrecipesfordinner  #easyrecipe #mealprep #highproteinrecipe #macrofriendlyrecipe #lowcalorierecipe #countingcalories #trackingmacros #fitness
author: stealth_health_life

subtitle.transcript: this crispy chicken sandwich is extremely simple to make at home, and it packs almost 50 grams of protein. and once you try it, you'll agree with me that it tastes way better than Chick Fil, A. Let me show you how to make it. grab one large chicken breast, tenderize until flatten, slice in half, season with salt and garlic powder. now, we need to build the breading stations. station one is flour, salt, garlic and pepper. next, egg whites and hot sauce, and for the crispy exterior, we're gonna use corn flakes. crush them up just a little bit. dunk your chicken in the flour, egg mixture and press into the corn flakes. press it down to make sure it's fully coated. hit it with a light oil spray, toss in the air fryer and flip halfway, lightly toast some brioche buns. top with this low calorie sriracha sauce using these ingredients on screen. finish with pickles and your crispy chicken.

title: ⚡️FOR THUNDER THIGHS⚡️ Here’s how you can train hamstrings intelligently 1️⃣ Typically I’ll train them 2 days per week. Day 1 is a lying leg curl + a stiff leg deadlift variation. Day 2 is often only a seated curl (this is because it on my more quad focused leg day) 2️⃣ Everything is usually for 3-4 sets in the 6-12 rep range with at least 3 minutes of rest between each set 3️⃣ If I’m doing both a leg curl and a SLDL variation in the same workout, I’ll usually start with the leg curl. In which case, it’ll be a lying leg curl (Lying leg curls will train the hamstrings in their short position & SLDL’s will train them in their lengthened position. subtitle.transcript: here is the simplest set of steps for a perfect deadlift that you will ever see first approach the bar so that your shins are one inch away from the barbell placing the bar directly over the middle of your foot and then slightly turn your toes outward the width of your stance should be the same that you would use for a maximal vertical jump step 2 without bending your knees forward bend over and grab the barbell just on the outside of your legs when you do this there should still be an inch between your shins and the bar step 3 bend your knees forward until your shins meet the barbell dropping your hips down into position step four flatten your back think about dropping your belly down between your legs you should feel a little bit of the weight of the bar in your hands fix your eyesight on an object 12 to 15 feet in front of you push your knees out into your forearms and then drag the barbell directly up your legs until you're standing straight up with your hips pushed through your chest pushed through and your shoulders held back then lower the bar the exact same way that you picked it up down your legs and to the floor this is known as the starting strength method hope it helps

title: Could you survive this 🤔 #fitness #gym #school
author: yourdailyfill

subtitle.transcript: People are shocked at what American high school gym class look like in the 19 60s. This footage is from one of the 4000 US high schools that followed LA Sierra physical education program that was pushed to be the standard model by JFK. According to the LA Sierra Physical Education Standards that were outlined in their 1966 handbook, the minimum push UPS that a student should be able to do is 16 and they should have at least a 7 and 1/2 minute mile run. Considering most modern Americans struggle to even complete 5 push UPS, this 16 minimum is quite shocking. The top group that was outlined in the handbook is Blue Team, and to be a part of this you had to be able to preform 12 handstand push UPS and at least 14 pull UPS, which are crazily impressive standards considering one in 6 modern American children have obesity. It is a shocking sight to see how seriously fitness and health were being taken in the 19 60s and how even the president was helping push forward this higher standard of physical education in school. Many people wonder if America as a country will ever return to a place even close to this, but considering the trends in obesity and the culture shift of America, it continues to seem unlikely.

title: How to fix skinny fat ✅ #wilsoncoaching #GymTok #gymtiktok #Fitness #gym
author: shivwilsonn

subtitle.transcript: So skinny fat basically means you have a low amount of muscle mass and a higher than average body fat percentage. So being in a calorie deficit and doing loads of cardio is not the answer to your problem, darling, because this is only gonna make the problem worser, worser, worser. And because you already don't have a lot of muscle mass, you losing body fat is not gonna give you that lean, tone, defined look that you're looking for. So how do you fix it? Body recomp. So first of all, we're gonna stop doing loads of cardio and we're gonna focus on lifting weights to actually help you build some muscle. So get in the gym three to four times a week and lift heavy. And rather than eating less food, eat at your maintenance or a slight calorie surplus of around 5 to 7% of what your maintenance calories are, and aim for 1 gram to 1.5 grams of goal body weight each day. So let's say you wanna weigh 130 pounds. You're gonna need to eat 130 grams of protein each day. Because the goal here isn't just to look smaller, it's to be lean, strong, and actually have some shape and definition to your physique. You don't need to lose weight, you need to rebuild your body from the inside out. You don't fix skinny fat by getting skinnier, you fix it by getting stronger.

title: Are energy drinks killing you? Probably not Aside from caffeine, the ingredients that are in one sugar-free energy drink are nowhere near the amounts that would be considered harmful I’m not promoting these as a “health” drink But the fear around them is wildly misplaced Caffeine is by far the ingredient you should pay the most attention to because of its effects on heart rate and blood pressure But even then, the 160mg in one can isn’t remotely unusual considering a simple coffee from Starbucks can contain over 400mg+… You don’t have to drink these But we should at least stop pretending they’re somehow uniquely toxic #fitness #gym #energydrinks #celcius #whitemonster
author: trainbloom

subtitle.transcript: By now, I think everyone agrees that these are horrible for you. But what if everyone's wrong? This is the chemical makeup of one sugar free monster. Most of them are harmless, like water, electrolytes, or vitamins. But four stick out. That have been linked to cancer, heart attacks, and kidney disease. The first and most dangerous is actually caffeine. One can has 160 mg, which sounds like a lot until you realize this large coffee from Starbucks has over 400, the max recommended daily intake. You get more AK in this 1 cup of vanilla Greek yogurt, more citric acid in this one orange, and more taurine in a small cut of tuna. So are all of these dangerous? Well, no, because nothing is dangerous until it's taken in the wrong amount. Even something as clean as water will kill you if you drink too much of it. The dose is what makes the poison. And the way scientists figure out what the safe dose of these ingredients is, is by first finding the highest amount you can still consume where nothing bad happens. In research called the N O A E L. And to create our safe daily intake limit, they divide that number by another hundred to create a massive safety buffer. And even then, when you look at the highest dosed ingredient out of all these, besides caffeine, it's still even 40 times lower than that. And that doesn't mean these are harmless. Caffeine is the One thing that some people genuinely need to be mindful of. But other than that, none of these ingredients should scare you at the dose found in one energy drink.

title: What does Jacobs ladder improve? Well… a lot? // #fitness #workout #gym
author: chaysembyrd

subtitle.transcript: I did Jacob's Ladder every day for one week instead of running, and here's what's different. First and foremost, I wanted to do this because the first time I ever use this ladder, it was genuinely one of the most fun forms of cardio I've ever done. It also felt like I was working out harder, but using a lot less effort than I would have if I was running on the. But before I begin my testing trials, I did a little bit of googling to see what other benefits there are to using Jacob's Ladder, and here is what the internet told me. It's a full body, low impact workout. So if you are prone to joint, tendon, and or knee issues and you can't do cardio like running or maybe even the Stairmaster, this could be a great alternative because you're softly hitting the ladder steps as opposed to running on a treadmill or pavement where you are pounding and placing a lot of impact on your joints. So using this is a great combination of maintaining that low impact workout while still being in that high intensity range. Now, after doing this for six workouts, I can confirm it does do all of that plus more. During each workout, I could feel my chest, shoulders, quads, glutes, core, calves, and hamstrings being used. Every muscle was burning. And not like a, oh, I need to stop kind of way, but in a, oh, I'm getting a Really good workout in kind of way. It also really challenged my hand eye coordination. It really improved my grip strength and obviously my endurance as well. Not to mention I was left with a sick pump after each session. Also realized that the lower you are in the latter, the more resistance there is. So I can focus on strength, but the the higher up you go means less resistance, but you could focus on your endurance. Overall, I recommend you all try this because it is genuinely a fun form of cardio.

title: High Protein Honey Garlic Butter Chicken Mac n Cheese!🍗🍯🧀 Absolutely one of the best combos, so indulgent, bursting with flavour and packed with 60g of protein! Macros Per Serving (4 Total) 597 Calories | 59g Protein | 52g Carbs | 16g Fat Ingredients (Makes 4) Honey Garlic Chicken - 800g Raw Chicken Breast cut into cubes - 1.5 Tsp Salt - 1 Tsp Black Pepper - 1 Tsp Chilli Flakes (leave it out if you don’t want it spicy) - 1.5 Tsp Garlic Powder - 1.5 Tsp Onion Powder - 1.5 Tep Paprika or Smoked Paprika - 2 Tsp Olive Oil - 30g Light Butter (Brand: Lurpak) for cooking + extra once cooked - 2 Tsp Minced Garlic - 30g Honey (15g Honey per batch of chicken) - Handful Fresh Chopped Parsley Get a pan on medium heat first then add butter. Let it melt then add your chicken (don’t overcrowd the pan). Cook for 4-5 mins on one side first till you get a nice golden brown crust. Then cook the other side for 3-4 mins more. Lower the heat completely when adding the extra butter, garlic and honey. Mix till well coated and sticky then set aside Garlic Mac n Cheese - Big Tbsp Minced Garlic - 300ml Skimmed Milk - 160g Light Cream Cheese (Brand: Philadelphia) - 1 Tsp Salt or to taste - 1/2 Tsp Black Pepper - 1 Tsp Smoked Paprika - 1/2 Tsp Nutmeg (adds a great deep flavour!) - 100g Low Fat Cheddar Cheese (You can use any low fat cheese you have available) - 220g Uncooked Macaroni Pasta or any pasta of your choice On medium low heat cook the minced garlic in the residue butter of the chicken for 2 mins till fragrant. Then add milk, cream cheese, spices. Mix this till completely smooth then lower the heat before adding the cheddar cheese. Stir till it melts then add your cooked macaroni and give it a good mix then Serve & ENJOY! . . . . #garlicbutter #honeygarlic #chicken #chickenrecipes #macncheese #macaroni #pasta #macandcheese #highprotein #mealprep #foodie #healthyrecipes #weightloss #lowcalorie #eathealthy #fitness #mealprepideas
author: jalalsamfit

subtitle.transcript: The most delicious high protein Honey, Garlic Butter Chicken, Mac and cheese all for 590 calories. Packed with flavour. So easy to make and perfect to meal prep for the week. Slice your chicken into cubes. Season with salt, black pepper, chilli flakes, garlic and onion powder, paprika and olive oil. Mix till the colour changes. Then cook the chicken on medium heat for 5 minutes each side till golden brown and crispy like this. Then lower the heat, add more butter, garlic, drizzle of honey and parsley. Give it a good mix till juicy and delicious. Then set the chicken aside. Add lots of garlic. Cook this for 2 minutes before adding low fat milk, light cream cheese and this extra seasoning. Stir till completely smooth. Then add low fat cheddar cheese. Keep stirring on low heat till it thickens. Then add your cooked macaroni. Now look how creamy and indulgent that looks. Finally your high protein meals are ready to serve and enjoy.

title: How to fix skinny-fat🙃 “Skinny-fat” is confusing? Because the more weight you try and lose, the worse the problem seems to get? That’s usually because people are trying to solve the wrong problem💡 The problem most people *think* they need to solve is having too much body fat. They try and solve this by: - adding endless cardio - and restricting food more and more But that’s only going to make the problem worse Because “skinny-fat” doesn’t usually come from not having too much body fat, it comes from not having enough *muscle* underneath our fat to give us any shape or definition. To fix this, you would want to: - Focus on lifting heavy weights - Actually limit your cardio (probably not more than 1/3 of your total exercise) - And often times actually eat *more* food, not less It’s also important to note that every human body is different, so the exact solution for each person will be a little bit different - but this generally a good place to start 🤘🏼 #skinnyfat #abs #coreworkout #cardio #FitTok
author: trainbloom

subtitle.transcript: Skinny fat is confusing because the more cardio you do and the less food you try and eat, the worse the problem seems to get. And that's because you're trying to solve the wrong problem. Any fat doesn't come from having too much body fat. It comes from not having enough muscle to give your body that lean, tone, or defined look you're going for. There's always going to be a layer of fat on top of your muscle. That's how our bodies are set up. And if you don't have any lean muscle to go underneath that fat, there's nothing to give your physique any shape, which is where tone comes from. You can lower your body fat as much as you want. It'll never be enough to make up for the lack of muscle underneath. So instead of adding more cardio, focus instead on lifting heavy weights. It won't make you bulky, I promise. And about 1g  of protein per pound of desired body weight. I have a free protein calculator in my bio if you want a more personalized number. title: The dumbbell bench press is arguably the best exercise for building your chest! #GymTok #fyp #FitTok
author: jeremyethier

subtitle.transcript: dumbbell bench press is arguably the best exercise for building your chest. but to better target the chest and avoid shoulder injury, you want to avoid making this mistake. many people use a very wide arm path and press the weight up and down. this can not only increase the risk of shoulder discomfort and potential injury, but it also just doesn't stimulate the chest very well. instead, to maximize chest activation. you want your arm path to line up in the same direction that most of the chest fibers run to do this, tuck your elbows to about a 45 to 60 degree angle away from your body and allow your grip to turn in slightly with your elbows. just keep in mind that when you apply this form, the dumbbells will no longer move straight up and down but rather forwards on the way down towards your mid chest and backwards on the way up towards your shoulders. don't be afraid to lighten the weight as well to ensure that you're using the correct form. try this out in your next workout and you'll feel the difference right away and give me a follow for more tips just like this.

title: Hate to burst your bubble (or maybe rings in this case? lol) But any device that tells you how many calories you burned during a workout is simply not even close to the truth. (p.s. congrats sam, you killed it this weekend) Devices like the Apple Watch, Whoop, Oura, etc. are great for certain things (e.g. step count, sleep data, recovery) But they suck for figuring out how many calories you burn Yes, the technology in these devices has gotten better since this study came out a few years ago… But the technology isn’t why they’re innacurate Here’s what the calorie tracking device takes into account to give you an estimate of how many calories you burn: - Heart rate - Gender - Weight - Age - Workout type But what it would take to *accurately* estimate how many calories you burn during a workout is all of that, PLUS 100+ other things that these devices can’t take into account… Things like your hormone profile and genetics, to even more ridiculous things like the temperature of the room you’re in or how much sleep you got last night… But that’s okay… Because knowing *exactly* how many calories you burned in one workout doesn’t really matter The amount of calories you burn in your workouts is <5% of what you burn in an entire week So if you’re trying to lose weight, adjusting your calorie intake day by day doesn’t really make any sense And it would make a lot more sense by just paying attention to your calorie intake and comparing it to how your scale is moving over time e.g. if you are eating 2,200 calories consistently, and the scale isn’t moving, then 2,200 is around your maintenence and you should either eat below that or increase how many calories you burn in a day to get into a deficit Study mentioned in reel: PMID: 28538708 #FitTok #GymTok #Running
author: trainbloom

subtitle.transcript: Cause when I see somebody wearing an Apple Watch and they post it after their workout. Really? You burned 1,500 calories in an hour? Exactly how inaccurate are these? Well, lucky for us, Stanford researchers wanted to find out. They took seven of the most popular wrist worn calorie tracking devices and put them on people for a few different workouts to see how accurate they really were. And the results even shocked the researchers, because although these things were accurate at measuring things like your heart rate and step count, when it came to measuring calories, even the best one was off by almost 30% and the worst off by 93%. Meaning if a tracker says you burned 1,000 calories during a workout, you might have only burned a few hundred. And yeah, technology has gotten better since this study came out a few years ago, but the technology wasn't the problem. The real issue is that these devices only use about five metric to come up with that number, where in reality there are hundreds that influence how many calories you burn, things these devices can't take into account. But that's all okay, because knowing exactly how many calories you burn during a workout doesn't really matter. And there are way more important numbers to pay attention to if you want to lose weight.

title: Twinkies make you… healthy?   Not quite 💔 (even though that’s what half the comments will tell you that’s what I’m saying) Sometimes you need extreme examples to highlight a point Should anyone eat like this to lose weight? No—short term health improvement is not the same thing as long term health outcomes  But there are 3 BIG lessons I think you can take from the experiment in this video: 1. A calorie deficit isn’t *a* way you lose weight, it’s *the* way you lose weight 2. Simply getting to a healthy body weight and not carrying excess body fat will probably do more for your health than any “optimal” diet would staying at a higher body fat level 3. And as terrifying as some influencers make certain “junk” foods sound for your health, there’s really no such thing as a healthy or unhealthy food - only a healthy or unhealthy diet as a whole. Someone who’s diet consists of 95% fast food that eats one salad isn’t “healthy” And someone who eats mostly whole, minimally processed foods having a donut for a snack isn’t “unhealhty” On top of all of this, its a nice remider that your diet only accounts for roughly ~20% of your overall health Things like your body composition, how much strength you have, how active you are, how well you sleep, and how well you manage your stress, along with 100+ other things also go into it And yes, I know what you’re thinking… This is just one guy who did a self experiment, you can’t use this as evidence Which I agree with But there is PLENTY of research showing that simply reducing body fat levels, regaradless of how it’s done, improves so many different health metrics Like: - type 2 diabetes - hypertension (high blood pressure) - cholesterol and lipid levels - cardiovascular disease - improved glycemic control and reduced insulin resistance - and more (research linked below) ___ https://doi.org/10.7326/0003-4819-149-7-200810070-01004 PMID: 35457744 PMID: 28214525 PMID: 12055705 PMID: 21463847 PMID: 21593294 #gym #fittok #gymtok #weightloss #seedoils

title: Fat burning ≠ Fat loss 😯 Yes, there is such a thing as a “fat-burning zone” But no, it doesn’t matter at all when it comes to actually losing fat ☹️ There’s one BIG problem with thinking that spending more time in the “fat-burning zone” will result in more fat lost… When you burn more fat and less carbs during a workout, you just burn less fat and more carbs later in the day (and vice-versa) This happens because your body “calibrates” how much body fat and carbohydrates you burn over a 24-hour period so that you burn the same amount of each over time, regardless of what you burn during your workouts. For example: Whether you burn 500 calories doing sprints for 30-minutes, with most of those calories coming from carbs OR 500 calories from a 90 minute incline walk, with most of those calories coming from fat You’ll still burn about the same amount of body fat at the end of the day So basically, how much fat you *lose* in response to a cardio workout depends on how much it’s adding to your calorie deficit - not how much fat you burned for energy during the workout Fat *loss* comes down to storing less fat than you burn over time And that comes from whether or not you’re in a calorie deficit Incline walking IS NOT BAD!! I actually prefer it over sprints. It’s easier on the body, it takes less recovery, and for most people it doesn’t increase hunger that much - making it a great option if you’re trying to lose weight It’s just not inherently better than any other form of cardio for fat loss… It comes down to what you can be consistent with, and what you actually enjoy (or hate less lol) Studies/Research: 24-hour fat loss calibration: PMID: 15896087 #fittok #12330 #fatburner #gym
author: trainbloom

subtitle.transcript: You know that burning fat and losing fat aren't the same thing, right? Sprinting or walking? Let's explain this. When you exercise, your body can get energy from one of two places, either fats or carbs. And what it chooses to burn mostly depends on how hard you're working or what your heart rate is while doing it. For example, when you're doing something really intense like sprinting or lifting heavy weights, your body needs energy fast, so it uses carbs since they can be broken down more quickly. On the other hand, take longer to break down for fuel, so they're what's mostly used when doing something a little easier, like walking on the treadmill. knowing that just doing lower intensity workouts that burn more fat would make losing fat easier, right? Well, not quite. What people forget is that your body is pretty smart. So when you burn more fat and less carbs during a workout, your body ends up burning less fat and more carbs later in the day. And the same thing goes in reverse whether you burn 500 calories using mostly carbs by sprinting for 30 minutes, or mostly fat by walking on the treadmill for an hour and a half, at the end of the day your body will always burn around the same amount of total fat. Actually, losing fat only happens if you burn more than you store over time. And that comes down to whether or not you're in a Calorie deficit. There's nothing wrong with incline walking, it's just not better or worse than any other form of cardio for fat loss. At the end of the day, it comes down to what you enjoy the most or hate the least.

title: READ THIS FIRST!!! (pwetty plz🥺) This is a 60-second clip, from a full 60-minute podcast where we break down Strength Standards So let’s start by saying - there are countless other factors that go into how challenging an exercise is *other than just your height* The estimated 10-20% harder on the bench press (like stated in the video) is just one example of many used in the podcast That’s also assuming that the two individuals had: - the same exact amount of muscle mass - the same exact muscle insertion points - the same exact shoulder structure - the same exact joint angles - the same exact muscle belly lengths - the same exact other limb proportions - the same exact form/technique - and about 100 other metrics And where longer arms may be a disadvantage on bench press, they would be an advantage on deadlifts since it would shorten the range of motion making the deadlift a bit easier So I am NOT saying that being 2 inches taller makes every exercise you do 10-20% harder I am just highlighting that your skeletal anatomy plays a role in how strong you are The full podcast is live on Spotify, Apple Podcast, and YouTube if you want to listen more about how your anatomy affects your strength Added notes: 1. This is not a post about using height (tall or short) as an excuse or saying that one is inherently better than the other. This is to help understand basic biomechanics that you can implement into your own training routine based on your anatomy. For example: I generally have athletes with longer limbs work in lower rep ranges for bench press than those with shorter arms (i.e. 2-4 or 3-5 vs. 4-6 or 5-7 in strength training). This adjustment allows them to avoid building up excessive fatigue, recover, and perform better. Different exercises would have different adjustments based on other anatomical differences. One’s not better than the other, it’s data you can use to improve your approach, that’s all👍🏽 #tall #short #shortking #samsulek #fittok
author: trainbloom

subtitle.transcript: Here's how much just your height impacts how strong you are in the gym. So your bones act as levers when they're performing an exercise. And then the muscle is what provides the force that will move the lever against whatever weight it's working against. Let's take the bench press, for example. Your pack is the main muscle that's being used to move the levers against the weight of the barbell. If we take two people with the same exact amount of muscle mass, but we make one person's arm longer by just two inches, two things happen. First, the distance that weight now has to travel increases over the course of just 10 reps. The person with the longer arms will have to move that weight 20 more inches, or almost two feet further than the one with shorter arms. The second piece is something called torque, which, in the context of biomechanics, is just talking about how far the weight is from the main joint that's moving it. Elbow joint in this case. The further way that weight is from the joint, the more torque is gonna be required to move the same weight. So in this example with the bench press, the same exact weight will be anywhere from 10 to 20% harder for the person with just two extra inches on their arm.

title: "Calisthenics can't build muscle" - a gentlemanly debate. --- Calisthenics can absolutely build muscle, and you can use different variations to find the ideal difficulty for you. Interestingly, this might ESPECIALLY apply to larger lifters as well as smaller beginners. The larger people have more bodyweight attached to them (even if it's muscle). 10 pullups for a 250lb bodybuilder, for example, is awesome. And beginners generally have more room to grow, regardless of what they use. That said, there's no reason you can't or shouldn't use weights. Weights and machines offer new angles and positions that you make not be able to mimic exactly with bodyweight exercise. They allow you overload without changing your movement. This may be helpful to people who want to specialize in certain areas. However, it should be noted that you can develop an athletic physique with calisthenics and many have done so (for a variety of reasons).  This is part of a new "Arguing With Myself" series that emphatically argues different sides of an issue to (hopefully) give a slightly more nuanced understanding of it. The ones prior have been longer and it's hard to fit all important context into a Short. This one was fun to make though, and I used it to test my new mic. Have a great day! #homeworkout #hybridcalisthenics

title: Why are some people strong at one thing but "fail" at others?  I occasionally see people laughing at bodybuilders supposedly failing at doing muscle ups or even pushups. While these movements don't always look clean, I always think that they can learn them relatively quickly if they want. The foundation of strength and muscle may already be there.  Strength is at least somewhat skill specific. That's why if you stop doing a lift for a while, your numbers might drop and then rise rapidly when you start practicing it again.  A few potential lessons we can take from this:  1.) Our training should be close to what we want to improve. This can be anything from sport-specific movements to daily functions (think squatting for standing up, step ups for climbing stairs, running for running, etc.)  2.) We can add a few minutes of variations after our main workouts as accessories if we want to maintain a broader variety of skills while still focusing on our primary exercises. Mobility plays a large role here, so try to incorporate a large, full range of motion within at least some exercise.  The good news is that, with even small amounts of practice, there's more crossover than we might think. The example I gave of 400lb squats VS one-leg squats - sometimes this can be learned in a few sessions of practice. There are other factors like joint health and mobility, but this is covered under the specificity of training.  Sorry if some parts are not as clear as other times. Some parts of our team are sick this time of year, so we tried to do some simpler productions 😅. Still hope this can help. Have a wonderful day!  #hybridcalisthenics #homeworkout

title: Hamstrings 101 1️⃣ Typically, I’ll train them 2 days per week. Day 1 is a lying leg curl + a stiff leg deadlift variation. In which case, it’ll be a lying leg curl (Lying leg curls will train the hamstrings in their short position & SLDL’s will train them in their lengthened position. subtitle.transcript: This is the best guide you'll ever see on how to grow your hamstrings. You have 4 of them. First, the short head of the biceps femoris. It's the only hamstring muscle that doesn't attach to the hip, so when we bend at the knee, it's the only time it gets trained. So leg curls, seated or line, both likely work similarly well for growing it. For the other 3 hamstrings, seated will be superior for growth. Now here are the 3 variations you need to know. First, when you flare the toes out, preferentially targets the hamstring muscles on the outer portion of your leg, the long and short head of the biceps lmoris. Second, point them inwards and you'll preferentially utilize the hamstring muscles on the inner portion of your leg, the semi tendonosis and membranos. And 3rd, when you point them up, it'll spread the work more evenly across them all. This is what most people should do most of the time. Finally, training the hamstrings by hinging at the hip. This is the other way that you need to be training them. Here's what you need to know stiff leg deadlifts are the king. By keeping your knees pretty pretty much straight as you lower down, the hamstrings are stretched deeply across both joints and act like chains pulling down from the base of your pelvis until you're standing upright.

title: Leg extensions 🤝  ✅ make sure the machine is set up for your body, the back rest should be adjusted so that your knees line up with the pivot point, the ankle pad should be sitting at your ankles and set to the deepest range of motion.  ✅ next make sure your knees are lined up with your hips, you can do this by pointing your toes straight up, this will stop them from rotating out or inward and take tension off your knees.  ✅ keep your lower back and glutes glued to the back rest and seat, pull yourself down into it and engage your core, don’t over arch your lower back.  ✅ don’t just swing the weight around and use a ton of momentum, pick a weight that’s challenging but that you can control. This is the only machine that works your quads in the fully shortened position, so slow down your reps, really squeeze your quads at the top and then control the eccentric.  Save & try! 🫶 #legextensions  #legday #quads #formtips #gym #fitness
author: melmarrazzohall

subtitle.transcript: If your leg extensions look like this, listen up. First, you want to make sure that the machine is set up to your body. So you want your knees to line up with this pivot point here. And you want the ankle pad to be at a height where it's sitting right at your ankle and not on your feet. And you want it at the setting where you can get the deepest range of motion. And you wanna make sure that your glutes and your lower back stayed glued to the seat and the back rest the entire movement. A lot of people over arch their lower backs like this during this exercise. And this is a really unstable position for your pelvis to be in functionally. So instead what you can do is grab onto the seat, pull yourself into it and stack your ribs over your pelvis, really pulling that core tight. Lastly, you want to make sure that your feet are pointed straight up. This is gonna make sure that your knees are in line with your hips and they're not rolling out or rolling in. That's gonna place a lot of unnecessary tension on your knees. And don't just be swinging the weight around like this. Instead, move slowly, control every rep, pause at the top before releasing down. title: L sit is the fundamental exercise for calisthenics. This is my workout which helped me to unlock it.  #calisthenics #lsit #fitnessmotivation
author: cali.hoss

subtitle.transcript: Before you learn the human flag or handstand, you should first master the L sit. It's one of the fundamental movements in calisthenics, not only physically demanding, but also mentally challenging. The first exercise is Jefferson Curls. They are great for improving hamstring flexibility and developing strength in the posterior chain. Next are laying leg raises with resistance. This exercise is ideal if hanging leg raises are too difficult. I start by doing them for reps to build dynamic strength, then hold for time to develop static strength. The fourth exercise is seated leg lifts. They put even more emphasis on compression and hip engagement. During the exercise, focus on squeezing your core as much as possible. After that, I do the same movement, but over yoga blocks to increase the range of motion. The final exercise is an isometric leg lift hold performed for time. Combine this routine with deep support holds and you will achieve your L sit in no time.

title: If you're like when I started...gym anxiety made you quiet working our and pursuing your fitness goals again and again. These are three facts that reduced my gym anxiety and finally got me consistent with working out. 1.) no one cares about you. i used to be super skinny and had a lot of gym anxiety. i felt like i was embarrassing myself by going to the gym not looking fit. years later, i now know that 99% of people do not even see you. everyones trying to get in and out of the gym because they have somewhere to be and are busy. plus think about it: how many people are really thinking about you when they're in the middle of lifting really challenging weights? sometimes i cant even remember how many reps i did 2.) progress takes time. i gave up so many times bc i didnt look any different a few weeks into working out. it really sucks because if i kept at it for longer than 1-2 months i would've started seeing so much growth from then on out 3.) use videos. not knowing if i looked stupid doing an exercise wrong really messed with my confidence at the gym. but thats why i make videos explaining exercise form to yall. theres also soooo many videos out there now for you to bring to the gym to watch and copy to master form! but just make sure to try your best to separate good info from the BS! #fitnessjourney #gymanxiety #confidence #gymmotivation #motivation #fitnessmotivation #gym #fitness

title: Grow Bigger Arms With This More Effective Tricep Exercise   🎥: @Brandon Maieli  #fitnessmotivation #bodybuilding #buildmuscle #musclegrowthtips #armworkout
author: anthonyanisimov

subtitle.transcript: If you want bigger arms, don't waste your time on tricep pushdown. Your triceps make up about 70% of your upper arm, meaning your triceps contribute more to the overall size and shape of your arm. The triceps have three heads, which is what others look at you like when you say, it's gonna be different this time. Lateral head, medial head, and this long one is the long head. The biggest and most important is the long head, which is what we wanna focus on, since it's the biggest and has the most potential for growth and to grow your long head. Just like maximizing the growth of any muscle, we wanna focus on getting it deep, deep stretch and tension. Instead of doing the pushdown, which doesn't stretch your long head and mostly hits your lateral head, which is a smaller muscle. Yours, not mine. A more effective exercise is the cable overhead tricep extension. I like using an easy bar attachment and setting the pin to about chest height. Get a nice stable base, come up slow on the way down at the bottom, hold that, stretch, repeat. If your elbows hurt or feel awkward, try the skull over, bringing it over your head. You get a little more freedom and flexibility with your joints, something you only had in your single days. Save this. Try either out. Once you get jacked and fill your arm sleeves better and can't even wear sleeves anymore, come back and Hit that follow button.

title: From flat to full — build a complete chest 💪 Incline ➝ Flat ➝ Flyes. Control every rep, finish strong. #chestworkout #fitonomycoach #strengthtraining #musclebuilding #fitnessmotivation
author: fitonomy.coaching

subtitle.transcript: From flat to full, build your complete chest. First, hit the upper chest. Go incline. Use the incline barbell bench press. Do not lower the bar to your neck, but to your chest for maximum activation. Now go to the incline dumbbell press. Don't keep elbows at 90 degrees. Bring them slightly in to protect shoulders. Next, load a high cable flies. Keep elbows slightly bent and squeeze at the top. Moving to the rest of the chest. Go with the flat barbell press. Keep the wrist neutral. Then cable flies with a slight lean forward. Keep it tight. Control every rep. Don't leave now. The most important part is coming. To get full growth, you can't skip this. Machine flies. Don't drop your body lower than the handles. Think of it like hugging a big tree. Chest tall and arms wrapping around. That's what gives your chest the round, complete look. Stay consistent, save this and you'll build a full chest.

Day 2 legs quad focus, 1 squat exercise, 1 quad isolation, 1 hamstring, 1 calf, 1 AB workout. Day 3 upper back focus. Two back exercises, one pulling horizontally, one pulling vertically, two shoulder exercises, one chest. Day four legs again. One exercise where you hinge and bend that ass over. One leg pressing exercise, one glute focus, one calf, one AB workout. Day five upper shoulder focus. subtitle.transcript: This is how I dead ass got consistent in the gym, lost 45 pounds, and now I'm shredded. This is not gonna be an aesthetic clean girl thing. This is just no bullshit. What worked for me. I stopped waiting to be motivated. There is no motivation. There is discipline. And I integrated it into my everyday part of my routine. Okay? Just like brushing my teeth, going to the gym. Non negotiable. I stopped doing workouts that I hated. I'm 5 9, I'm taller, so some workouts that might work really well for me might not work for other people who are shorter. So I had to learn and find the workouts that were best for me and what I love the most. Like, if you hate something, why are you forcing it? Find something that you love and you wanna do. And I stopped trying to be perfect. I think the issue with me is I give it a all or nothing mentality. So I had to learn that I am human, okay? It's all about consistency in the long term. Not if you have a slip up here and there. Having a little slip up does not mean that you fail. You're a human. It's okay. I promise. Once I let go of the all or nothing mindset, everything started to click. And now it's something that I love and I enjoy doing, and lifting is. It just makes me feel so happy and I need to Do it every day. Consistency is not about being perfect. It's about showing up when you don't want to. And it will pay off. I promise.

author: nicofelich

subtitle.transcript: this is how to run longer distances. a lot of people say they can't run more than 2 miles, but I'm telling you, you can. I went from always tapping out at about 3 miles to being able to run 26.2 miles. and here's how the most important thing is to stop tracking mileage in order to train your body to be able to last longer on runs. you need to build your aerobic base. the way you do this is by spending more time running. the reason you shouldn't track mileage at the beginning is because when you have in your head a set amount of miles, you gotta get done, your natural instinct is to get them done as fast as possible. this will just make you burn out too quick. instead, set your timer for 45 minutes. go as slow as you need to, but run the whole time. it's gonna feel weird at first. you're gonna feel like you're going way too slow and you're gonna wanna go faster. but you gotta trust the process. remember to build your aerobic base. you gotta be running for a longer period of time, even if it's slow. after I started doing this consistently for a while. that's when I started worrying more about my mileage and my pace. you gotta lay the foundation before you put the house on top of it.

subtitle.transcript: 3 signs you might be an ectomorph. Sign No. 1 is that you have skinny wrists or skinny joints in general. This is because ectomorphs are defined by not only people that have low muscle mass, but also have low bone density, which is why ectomorphs usually have a narrow chest, giving them a rectangular frame. Sign No. 2 is if you need to eat around 30, five hundred calories just to gain weight. Most people can eat a few extra calories and they'll gain weight. But as an ectomorph, because you have a very fast metabolism, you need to eat way above average just to gain a few pounds. So you track calories not to lose weight, but to simply make sure you're eating enough, which brings you to sign No. 3. You never have to go on a cut simply because you never had to. You always maintain low body fat percentage and struggle to put on muscle. your focus has always been to gain weight and be on that forever bulk. If I just described you, then you're probably an ectomorph.

subtitle.transcript: I've been able to round out the sides of my glutes by focusing more on glute minimus dominant exercises instead of glute medius. This has made a huge difference in preventing that square look from the back. Here are a couple exercises that help. The first exercise is side lying hip abductions. A big form cue here is foot position. Make sure your foot is pointed slightly towards the ground. This shifts the emphasis away from the glute medius and makes this a great alternative to the hip abduction machine. The next exercise is single leg glute bridges. These are very beginner friendly and perfect if single leg hip thrusts feel too complicated or unstable. They still help build glute shape and control one side at a time. The last exercise is standing hip abductions. These can be progressed from side lying hip abductions, or you can rotate both. I personally used to do side lying hip abductions on the glute focus days and standing hip abductions on hamstring days. One important form tip with standing abductions make sure your foot is pointed slightly inward. If it's point it outward, you'll accidentally shift the work back to the glute medius. title: What's the BEST workout routine & how many days should you workout? 👇  Anyone that gives you a straight up answer isn't always right. In reality, it depends. We all recover at different rates, require different amounts of weekly volume, and all train differently. Taking this into account, there is no best workout routine. But that doesn't mean you can't make your workout routine the best for you. Doing so actually makes you find way more progress not only because you're literally optimizing your routine, but also because yiu're able to be really consistent with it.  1.) Find the right amount of weekly set volume (somewhere between 6-20 weekly sets per muscle group) you need to recover fully from each workout while still challenging yourself.  2.) Find how many days a week you can be realitically most consistent with. Whether it's 4,5,6 times a week, space out rest days accordingly to be able to recover from your previous workouts to prevent any performance issues. Then assign a variety of splits: Push Pull Legs (6 days), Push Pull Legs Upper Lower (5 days), Upper Lower (4 days) 3.) Find exercises that are smarter than others and effective at targeting the muscle you're aiming to target.  4.) Now that you have the workout routine, sets, and exercises, it all comes down to finding a good rep range for your exercises. Any rep range between 6-15 is ideal. I personally love 6-8 or 6-10 for most of my exercises. You're welcome. You're welcome. Now you've got almost everything it takes to actually have the BEST workout routine. All it takes now is to test and fine tune 😌 #fitnesstips #workoutroutine #workoutplan #gymtips #buildingmuscle

subtitle.transcript: shoulder pressing here are the main mistakes that I see and how to fix them first mistake is having the bench completely upright ideally we want it at 75 or 60 degrees this puts the front of the shoulder in a better position to work as you go throughout that range next mistake is half repping at the top of the range typically it looks like this your shoulders can still work from here to here so for a full range of motion start with the dumbbell on the shoulders pressing up and slightly closer together finishing in a y shape not an eye shape this is another common mistake I could hold this all day because I've lost tension on the shoulders the force of a dumbbell is straight down so if I finish here my shoulder joint takes the load if I finish here the muscles still take the load now this mistake could save you from an it's common for people to press with their elbows too wide which can also be the reason for that limited range of motion instead drop the elbows in 15 to 30 degrees press straight above the shoulders keeping your elbows slightly tucked allows you to stay within the scapular plane so when pressing from here this is the smoothest range of motion or your shoulder joint bonus always try and keep your wrist aligned on top of the elbow this way we get a better force transfer

author: squatuniversity

subtitle.transcript: yeah, if you want to squat big weight with excellent technique, here's a 4 step process to follow. remember, how you start leads to how you finish. as you get under the bar, you're going to stack your torso, open your hips, and wedge yourself against the bar. create 1t of torso stiffness. big breath, then stand up with the bar controlled, steps back. once you get set up in your squat stance, you're then going to establish a good, firm foundation again. so ribs stacked on top of the pelvis, tripod foot set up. spread your body weight across these 3 points. once you're set up well, you're then going to take a big breath into your lateral stomach. you'll feel that area expand, create 1t of torso stiffness, and then descend under control all the way into the bottom position. remember, your arms in line with your torso.

author: eloraagummerson

subtitle.transcript: How often should you train your glutes to grow them as effectively as possible? When you train a muscle, you're essentially breaking down the muscle tissue, and after the workout your muscles recover and adapt, growing a bit bigger and stronger than before. It generally takes your muscles around 36 to 48 hours to recover. So if you're training your glutes once a week, that's not gonna be optimal, as they'll be recovered and ready to go again around 48 hours after your workout. Therefore, we can say that twice a week is better than once. But if your trainer glutes too frequently, the muscle will actually decrease in size because you basically keep breaking down the muscle tissue before it's had a chance to fully recover. Therefore, two or three times a week would be optimal. And here are a few things to keep in mind. Aim for a total of 10 to 20 working sets per week for your glutes. Spread these sets out over two or three workouts, but don't increase the volume. The type of exercise you do will affect how long it takes for your muscles to recover. For example, it's gonna take your glutes longer to recover from a heavy Bulgarian split squat than a light glute kickback. Your due training experience will also affect your recovery. So if you're relatively new to training, I'd stick to twice a week and then switch it up in a few months.

title: 3 Fundamental terms you NEED to know about building muscle further explained👇 Progressive overload combines all the terms and is something you NEED to know in order to maximize your growth in the gym. How it works: Let's say you have 3 straight sets for bicep curls each with a rep range of 6-10 reps. The first set, you chose to do 20lbs and struggled to get 7 reps. The second set you did 20lbs and struggled to get 6 reps. The third set you did 20lbs and struggled to get 6 reps. You're near the bottom of your rep range (6-10), so you shoudn't increase the weight because your not strong enough yet. So bext time you do that same biceps exercise again, try and do more reps of the same weight. The day you're doing consistently 10 reps-ish on all three of your straight sets, you're ready to grab 22.5lbs and start that next session at the bottom of the rep range at 6 reps again. Rinse and repeat to get stronger and maximize growth. This is progressive overload. Apply it to ALL exercises and muscles!  #progressiveoverload #workout #fitnesstips

title: You didn’t gain 2 lbs of fat overnight… To gain a pound of fat, you would need to be in a surplus of roughly 3500 calories. 5 x 3500 cals = 17,500 cals in one day. That’s a GNARLY food challenge that would require a lot of intention to accomplish, not eating a cookie one night 😂 There are SO many reasons that the scale can go up that is NOT fat gain: 👉Sodium. An excess of sodium causes you to hold water. 👉Sleep. Oversleeping OR undersleeping. 👉Stress. Stress increases cortisol & other fight-or-flight hormones that cause you to hold water. 👉Hard training session. The muscle cells are retaining more water for recovery. 👉Full glycogen stores.  1 gram of glycogen can hold 2-4 grams of water so when you eat carbohydrates and restore your glycogen levels, this can lead to an increase in scale weight that is actually advantageous. 👉Eating later than normal. It’s normal to wake up heavier after a night of later evening, simply because there is more food in your stomach. 👉Female hormone fluctuations. Need I say more😂 👉Sick. Inflammation is high to aid in recovery. 👉Lack of movement. This can also contribute to digestion changes. 👉Dehydration. Not drinking enough water can actually cause you to HOLD water. Before you go freak out and run to the elliptical to make up for the uptick in the scale (been there & done that too💁‍♀️) take inventory of ALLLL of the other things going on in your life before blaming it on your food! #fitness #nutrition #nutritiontips #FitTok #fitnesstips #fyp #foryoupage #weightloss #fitnesstransformation #fitnessjourney

title: Where does fat actually go when you burn it? You don’t sweat it out — you literally breathe it out. The real science of fat loss in 20 seconds. #FatLoss #FitnessTips #WeightLossScience #HealthFacts
author: flexplained101

subtitle.transcript: Ever wonder what actually happens to fat when you burn it? Spoiler, it doesn't melt and it definitely doesn't turn into muscle. When you move your body, you trigger a real process inside your fat cells. Your body needs energy, so it taps into stored fat, but it doesn't shrink the fat directly. Instead, fat cells release tiny molecules called fatty acids into your bloodstream. Those fatty acids travel to your muscles where they get broken down and used as fuel. And here's the crazy part most people don't know. Most of the fat you lose actually leaves your body when you exhale. You literally breathe out the carbon from the fat you burned. Your lungs are as important as your workout. But to burn fat efficiently, your body needs two things, a small calorie deficit and consistent movement. Not endless sweating, just steady activity that raises your energy demand.

subtitle.transcript: Did you cut or bulk? If you have this physique, the answer is actually none. You should actually do something called a body recompensation. With this physique, you have some fat and you're lacking muscle. So if you eat in a calorie surplus and you bulk, yes, you'll gain muscle, but you'll gain some fat as well. And on the other side, if you eat in a calorie deficit and you cut, you'll lose fat, but you also won't gain that much muscle. But a body recomposition allows you to do both at the same time. So instead of eating in a surplus or a deficit, you're eating at your calorie maintenance while also eating 0.8 grams of protein per pound of body weight. This allows you to replace fat mass with lean body mass. And so you'll achieve that goal of losing fat but also building muscle at the same time.

subtitle.transcript: This is the bench press sticking point. The sticking point is the slowest point on the bar path where you experience the weakest activation. This is usually where you fail your press. Everyone will have a different sticking point because this can depend on body mechanics, muscle imbalances and technique. Here are the three sticking points as well as what you can do to address them. First sticking point is off the chest. Failing off your chest is an indicator of weak pec muscles and can also occur as a result of your chest caving in, slowing down too much on the descent or being too reliant on bouncing the bar off your chest. Good way to address this sticking point is by adding pauses to your bench press training, increasing your explosiveness to move the bar as fast as possible and to isolate the strength of your pecs on other exercises. Second sticking point is the mid range sticking point. This is the range where your shoulders will be the limiting factor and can also be affected by whether your elbows flare out excessively or if you are too slow off your chest. To address this region, you wanna strengthen your shoulders on pressing movements, balance out your front and middle delts and utilize explosiveness to blow past the sticking point as fast as possible. The last and my own personal sticking point, the lockout sticking point. This is the range where your triceps are the limiting muscle group This one sucks the most because you do most of the work only to get blue bolts near the top. You want to isolate the strength of your triceps to address the sticking point and make sure your technique is in a good position to grind for your life. subtitle.transcript: Training every day is pointless if your weekly plan isn't set up right It's not just about your daily routine being well organized with the exercises sets and reps you need but also throughout the whole week which muscle you train each day For example, if on day one you do shoulders and triceps and on day two you train chest your chest workout will be weak because to work chest you need help from shoulders and triceps So, since those muscles are tired from yesterday's workout you can't give your best in chest Same goes for women who start by working glutes and the next day want to train the rest of their legs A correct weekly order could be Monday: chest and shoulders Tuesday: full legs Wednesday: back and biceps Thursday: shoulders and triceps And Friday: legs again This way, there's at least 48 hours rest between each muscle group it's important to keep that 48-hour break so the worked muscle can rest and recover properly If you notice in the previous example three days go by before a muscle group trains again within the same week But remember, this was just an example Everything should match your goals specific to each person That's why, using as an example a woman would restructure her weekly order in a different way to focus more on legs by splitting muscle groups and even having a specific training day just for glutes If you want to learn more about fitness Remember to save this video and follow me
